course_name_original: Fundamentals of thermodynamics and heat transfer (146175)
course_name_en: Fundamentals of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer
prerequisites: Solid background in basic disciplines such as mathematics and physics acquired by attending basic mathematics and physics courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Analyze thermodynamic systems, both closed and open, with particular attention to mass and energy balances.
Familiarize with the engineering issues of thermodynamics and heat transfer topics.
Understand and describe the basic modeling approach.
Develop a systematic problem-solving technique with particular attention to the importance of numerical calculation and the significance of figures.
Pursue a general energy management approach to analyze and investigate the role of energy analysis in industrial systems, energy plants, devices, and processes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and definitions of Thermodynamics.
Thermodynamic Systems: closed and open systems.
First Principle: First Principle for simple and cyclic transformations, specific heat, conservation of mass and energy.
Thermodynamic processes.
Thermodynamic diagrams.
State conditions for liquid and gaseous systems, saturation conditions.
Ideal gases: generality and equation of state; transformations of ideal gases.
Pure substances: generality and diagrams (p, v, T), (p, T) and (p, v) title of the vapor and liquid-vapor mixtures.
Second Principle: statements; reversibility and not reversible conditions, Carnot cycle, thermodynamic of reversible cycles.
The entropy quantity: its significance and properties as function of state.
Standard Air cycles: Otto, Diesel, Brayton-Joule and steam cycles.
The Rankine cycle with saturated and super-heated steam.
Inverse cycles (refrigeration cycles and heat pumps).
Heat transfer exchange mode. Introduction and definitions.
Conduction. The Fourier's law.
Thermal conductivity.
The Fourier equation.
Steady state conduction with and without heat generation.
Convection mode: generality, forced and natural convection.
Elements of dimensional analysis and correlations for the heat transfer coefficient calculation including example applications.
Transmittance of a wall and the global heat transfer coefficient.
Heat exchangers and the method of mean effective temperatures.
Fundamentals of radiation heat transfer.

assessment_methods.method: Written test (numerical exercises and oral questions/multiple-choice/demonstrations)
Oral interview (discussion and analysis of laboratory experiences, topics from heat transfer)

assessment_rules: The assessment includes a written test and an oral interview. The written test consists of numerical exercises and oral questions (multiple-choice or demonstrations) and is worth 75% of the grade. The oral interview is focused on discussing and analyzing submitted laboratory experiences and may include topics from heat transfer, making up the remaining 25%. Passing the written test is a prerequisite for the oral interview in the same session, otherwise the written exam is cancelled. An exemption allows students who pass the written exam in June to take the oral interview in July, but not later than the autumn session; laboratory reports must be submitted by the registration deadline for the July oral exam.
